'''''Guzmania lingulata''''', the '''droophead tufted airplant''' or '''scarlet star''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Bromeliaceae, subfamily Tillandsioideae. This [[evergreen]] [[epiphytic]] [[perennial plant|perennial]]<ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> is [[native plant|native]] to [[rainforest]] habitats in [[Central America]], northern and central [[South America]] and southern [[Mexico]].<ref name=x>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=247568 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref> The Latin word ''lingulata'' means "tongue-shaped".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref> The foliage grows in a star-shaped basal rosette culminating in an orange and red bracted [[inflorescence]].  It is among the most commonly cultivated bromeliad types, with [[cultivars]] producing flowers in shades of maroon, red, orange, yellow or pink.

==Varieties==
Four [[Variety (botany)|varieties]] are recognized:<ref name=x/>

*''Guzmania lingulata'' var. ''cardinalis'' <small>(André) Mez</small> – Colombia, Ecuador
*''Guzmania lingulata'' var. ''concolor'' <small>Proctor & Cedeño-Mald.</small> – Central America, West Indies, northern and central South America (Guianas and Colombia south to Bolivia), southern Mexico
*''Guzmania lingulata'' var. ''flammea'' <small>(L.B.Sm.) L.B.Sm.</small> – Colombia, Ecuador
*''Guzmania lingulata'' var. ''lingulata'' – Guyana, Suriname, Jamaica, Venezuelan Antilles; naturalized in Bermuda
